interpretation: The faster scalar is retained. Positive K and G make the frozen scalar block strongly hyperbolic with a common local time covector, so metric-cone straddling is not itself a local PDE failure or causal paradox. Global and matter-cone questions remain open.

theorem.canonical_reduction: H=K^(-1/2) G K^(-1/2) is symmetric positive definite, so an orthogonal U gives U^T H U=diag(c_1^2,c_2^2) with positive real eigenvalues.
theorem.common_time: The covector dt evaluates to -K on the scalar principal form and has g-inverse norm -1, so it is timelike for both scalar modes and the metric cone.
theorem.constant_coefficient_result: The scalar block has a positive conserved principal energy and a symmetric-hyperbolic first-order reduction; hence it is strongly hyperbolic at frozen constant coefficients.
theorem.decoupled_form: With q=K^(-1/2)U psi, the principal block becomes d_t^2 psi-diag(c_1^2,c_2^2) Laplacian psi=0.
hypotheses: K and G are real symmetric positive-definite constant matrices
the scalar principal equation is K d_t^2 q-G Laplacian q=0 in the aligned homogeneous rest frame
the background metric is locally diag(-1,1,1,1)
theorem.relation_to_straddling: When the active-gate theorem gives c_-^2<1<c_+^2, the faster mode remains real, finite, and governed by the same local time coordinate. Cone straddling is therefore not automatically a local hyperbolicity failure or causal paradox.
theorem.strict_limit: This does not establish a global time function, variable-coefficient strong hyperbolicity, causal compatibility with a disformal matter metric, or ultraviolet completion.
